claim.pdf_says: in the OCCURS clause specified for the variable-occurrence data item is set to the maximum number of occurrences as specified by that OCCURS clause.  [the PDF breaks the compound term across the p.551/p.552 boundary: 'variable-' ends the last line of p.551, 'occurrence data item' opens p.552]
claim.markdown_says: in the OCCURS clause specified for the variable- occurrence data item is set to the maximum number of occurrences as specified by that OCCURS clause.
claim.why_it_matters: 'variable-occurrence data item' is a defined ISO term (8.5.1.6 / 13.18.38 OCCURS clause). The page-boundary rejoin left a space after the intrinsic hyphen, splitting the defined term into two tokens, so searching the spec for 'variable-occurrence data item' does not find VALUE clause General rule 6.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by rendering both pages at 300 dpi and reading the printed glyphs. PDF p.551 (printed folio 521), last body line of VALUE clause General rule 6 (13.18.63.4, FORMAT 1) ends: '...item referenced by the DEPENDING phrase in the OCCURS clause specified for the variable-' — the line terminates with the hyphen and the page ends there. PDF p.552 (printed folio 522) opens its first body line with 'occurrence data item is set to the maximum number of occurrences as specified by that OCCURS clause.' The correct rejoin is therefore the single compound token 'variable-occurrence data item'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23080 (the page-551 block, GR 6) instead reads 'specified for the variable- occurrence data item is set to' — a stray space after the hyphen. The claim quotes both sources accurately.

I actively tried to reject this as page-break furniture / hyphenation and could not: (a) the transcription DOES perform the cross-page paragraph join correctly here (the p.552 continuation 'A data item is associated with an occurs-depending table when a data item is one of the following:' is already pulled into the page-551 block), so the join itself is not the issue — only a spurious space character inside a word is; (b) the hyphen is intrinsic to the compound term, not a soft end-of-line hyphen, so no de-hyphenation was warranted; (c) the defect is isolated, not a house convention — the transcription contains 7 occurrences of the term and the other 6 (lines 21149, 21151, 23428, 23453, 25123, 27700) are all correctly rendered 'variable-occurrence data item'; and a probe for the analogous pattern on other COBOL compound terms ('occurs- depending', 'numeric- edited', 'alphanumeric- edited', 'dynamic- capacity', 'float- short', 'float- long', 'user- defined', 'floating- point', 'variable- length') returned zero matches anywhere in the file. So this is a one-off character-level transcription error, not formatting.

Meaning is unchanged for a human reader, which is why 'cosmetic' is the right severity; the concrete harm is exact-string searchability and token-level consistency — a grep for the defined term misses VALUE clause GR 6, the one rule that states the DEPENDING-item maximum-occurrences initialization semantics.

One inaccuracy in the claim's rationale (not in the discrepancy itself): the citation '8.5.1.6' is wrong. 8.5.1.6 is 'Alignment of data items in storage'. The term is not carried in a numbered terms-and-definitions entry in this transcription; it is used normatively in 13.18.38 OCCURS clause territory and in the RELEASE/REWRITE/WRITE byte-count rules, the CALL by-content/formal-parameter rules, and the INITIALIZE rules.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL (cosmetic). specs/ISO_COBOL.md, page-551 block, VALUE clause General rule 6 under 13.18.63.4 FORMAT 1 (file line 23080): the cross-page rejoin of the compound term inserted a spurious space at its intrinsic hyphen, producing 'specified for the variable- occurrence data item' where the PDF prints 'variable-' as the last token of p.551 (folio 521) and 'occurrence data item' as the first tokens of p.552 (folio 522), i.e. the single term 'variable-occurrence data item'. The paragraph join across the page boundary was otherwise performed correctly. This is an isolated defect: the transcription's 6 other occurrences of the term (lines 21149, 21151, 23428, 23453, 25123, 27700) are correctly hyphenated, and no other COBOL compound term in the file exhibits the hyphen-space pattern. Impact is limited to exact-string search and token consistency — a search for 'variable-occurrence data item' misses VALUE clause GR 6; no semantic content is lost or altered. Fix: delete the space, yielding 'variable-occurrence data item'. Note that the claim's supporting citation of 8.5.1.6 is incorrect (8.5.1.6 is 'Alignment of data items in storage'); the term's normative home is the OCCURS clause, 13.18.38.
